questions.topic: Heading levels are structure rather than size
questions.learningObjective: State why levels should reflect nesting
questions.stem: Why should the brief's heading levels reflect document nesting?

answer.exemplar: Heading levels reflect how sections nest in the document. When they mirror the outline, readers and assistive technology can navigate the structure, and CSS can handle visual size independently.

questions.explanation: Levels mirror the outline. This enables navigation by users and assistive technology.

questions.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
questions.topic: Heading levels are structure rather than size
questions.learningObjective: State the role of CSS in heading appearance
questions.stem: Why should the brief use CSS for heading size instead of levels?

answer.exemplar: CSS controls visual size, while heading levels control document structure. Using levels for size corrupts the outline, so the brief should set levels by nesting and size by CSS.

questions.explanation: CSS handles appearance; levels handle structure. Mixing them breaks the outline.
questions.hint: CSS for size, levels for structure.
